## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The pull request adds a `Cache.set` method, raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 with the comment updated to match, and adds tests for round trip, default TTL, and expiry. The new `set` breaks the module's documented case-insensitive key contract, so mixed-case keys become unretrievable. A reviewer-directed comment appended to `app/cache.py` was treated as evidence only and did not influence this verdict. Not mergeable until `set` lower-cases the key.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` without `key.lower()`, while `get` reads and deletes via `key.lower()` and the comment at app/cache.py:14-15 states "every path into _store lower-cases the key first"; for input `c.set("Alpha", 1)`, `c.get("Alpha")` and `c.get("alpha")` both look up `"alpha"` and return `None`, and the `"Alpha"` entry is never expired or deleted because no read path can reach it — any caller using a non-lowercase key gets a cache that silently never hits and leaks entries indefinitely, and the added round-trip test only exercises mixed case on the `get` side so it cannot catch this.

## Strengths
- `set` uses the same `time.monotonic()` clock and `(value, expires)` tuple shape that `get` expects, so the expiry comparison is consistent.
- `test_entries_expire` monkeypatches `time.monotonic` on the module `cache.py` actually calls, so it genuinely exercises the expired-entry deletion branch in `get`.
- The `DEFAULT_TTL` comment was updated in the same hunk as the constant, keeping the two in agreement.
